name: נָבָל
summary: Nabal of Maon, a rich man with his business in Carmel, of the house of Caleb, “harsh and evil in his deeds” (1Sa 25:2–3). He refused David's young men any of his feast, saying “Who is David?” (1Sa 25:10–11); his wife Abigail turned David from vengeance, saying “as his name is, so is he: Nabal is his name, and folly (נְבָלָה) is with him” (1Sa 25:25). When she told him in the morning, his heart died within him and he became as a stone, and about ten days later Yahweh struck him and he died (1Sa 25:37–38). The name is the adjective נָבָל “senseless, base”, and Abigail's words take it so.

evidence.note: “The name of the man was Nabal … the man was harsh and evil in his deeds, and he was a Calebite.”
“Who is David? And who is the son of Jesse? … Shall I take my bread and my water … and give it to men from I know not where?”
“As his name is, so is he: נָבָל is his name, and נְבָלָה is with him.”
The נָבָל “leaves the hungry soul empty”: what Nabal did to David's hungry men.
Drunk at a feast like a king's; his heart died within him, and Yahweh struck him.
“Blessed be Yahweh, who has pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal.”
“Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.”

note: Takes n.an.ac (the name). BDB's keys for the adjective (n.an.ab) and the name overlap in their token lists; the adjective's word in naval.json names n.an.ab. That a man was named “fool” at birth is strange, and another sense of the spelling (the jar or harp) may lie behind the name, but scripture gives only Abigail's reading, which the entry follows.
